title: A LoRA layer from scratch
brief: Implement LoRA's forward pass, its parameter and memory accounting, the merge that makes it free at inference, and the best rank-r approximation of a matrix.
hints: lora_forward is x @ W.T + (alpha / r) * (x @ A.T) @ B.T. Keep the two matmul orders separate; do not form B @ A first unless you are implementing merge_lora.
merge_lora is W + (alpha / r) * (B @ A), the same shape as W. lora_forward(x, W, A, B, alpha, r) and x @ merge_lora(W, A, B, alpha, r).T should agree to machine precision.
optimiser_memory_bytes uses 16 bytes per trainable parameter in both modes; the mode argument documents which parameter count you are charging, it does not change the rate.

best_rank_approximation: numpy.linalg.svd(delta_w, full_matrices=False) gives U, s, Vt with s sorted descending. Truncate all three to the first r components and reconstruct U[:, :r] @ diag(s[:r]) @ Vt[:r, :].

For the gradient-direction check: with L = 0.5 * ||merge_lora(W, A, B, alpha, r) - target||^2, the gradient with respect to the effective weight is G = merge_lora(...) - target, and the chain rule through BA gives dL/dA = (alpha/r) * B.T @ G, dL/dB = (alpha/r) * G @ A.T.
